label: identity_ready
title: Server identity baseline
body: Two account identities and two device keys enter as finite existing or unregistered records. Device grants and account-session authority are separate.

label: identity_challenge
title: Stored sign-in challenge
body: Native starts store a verifier challenge without account authority. Wallet and NEAR AI starts persist ceremony bindings. Local cancellation abandons the wait without deleting the server record. Expiry and process restart have different effects.

label: identity_browser
title: Browser confirmation and native callback
body: A browser login link stores its account and tenant. Confirmation consumes a live link and creates a browser session. A live native request also receives a one-time code; a missing native request leaves the browser login successful.

label: identity_verifying
title: Single-use take and saved bindings
body: The server takes the code or ceremony before checking saved verifier, request identity and device bindings. Failed evidence or unavailable external verification can leave a consumed handle without a session.

label: identity_result
title: Committed session and response
body: An issued session is durable before its response arrives. A lost response does not roll back the session. Provisioning key conflicts and revocation are separate from response delivery.

label: identity_authority
title: Authenticated request and token rotation
body: Credential transport, tenant, stored account, presented token and token generation are separate. Validation saves the request authority, canonical token and rotation eligibility from its SELECT; a later clock boundary does not change that plan. A planned rotation can lose a race with another rotation or revocation. Native sessions remain weak account authority. Native bearer transport requires a native-kind row; cookie transport can also validate a native-kind row, while retaining cookie transport and weak authority. A wrong-kind native bearer may update last-seen or rotate the row during database validation before the resolver refuses authority and withholds the rotated token. Mixed credentials and device bearers are refused before database validation.

label: identity_revocation
title: Session and device revocation
body: Current-session logout, account-wide session revocation and device revocation change different records. Device revocation also ends grants and attributed sessions, plus other live unattributed native sessions, while sparing the caller when unattributed.

label: identity_headless
title: Headless device codes and renewal
body: A native account session can mint a code by signing with an independently supplied linked minter key, including when the session has no device attribution. A key that joined by code cannot mint another code. Successful redemption atomically links a device and issues its session. Only a code-linked device may renew with its key; a renewal nonce remains separate from a session token.
